entries.name: Maximum groundspeed
entries.evidence: The single figure, both units as printed: 87 knots / 100 mph.

entries.name: Maximum altitude above ground level
entries.evidence: 400 feet, and the 400-foot structure radius and 400-foot above-structure allowance as three distinct figures.

entries.name: Minimum flight visibility
entries.evidence: 3 statute miles, plus the section's own definition of flight visibility, which is a definition and not a threshold.

entries.name: Minimum distance from clouds
entries.evidence: Both figures: 500 ft below, 2,000 ft horizontal. A single combined value would lose the distinction.

entries.name: Civil twilight, outside Alaska
entries.evidence: Both windows: 30 minutes before official sunrise to sunrise, and sunset to 30 minutes after.

entries.name: Groundspeed is within the limit
entries.evidence: At, just below and just above 87 knots. The printed mph figure is a rounding of the knots figure; test which one governs.

entries.name: Altitude is within the limit
entries.evidence: The plain 400 ft AGL case; inside a 400 ft radius of a structure; and the boundary where the aircraft is within the radius but above the structure's uppermost limit plus 400.

entries.name: Visibility and cloud clearance are met
entries.evidence: Each minimum independently, and the case where one passes and the other fails.

entries.name: Only one aircraft is operated at a time
entries.evidence: One aircraft; two aircraft; the same person acting as visual observer for a second.
entries.note: 2020 wording bars a person who may 'operate'; the later wording bars one who may 'manipulate flight controls'.

entries.name: Controlled airspace requires prior ATC authorization
entries.evidence: Each of Class B, C, D and the lateral surface area of Class E, with and without authorization; and Class G, which needs none.
entries.note: The airspace class is an input. Determining it from a position requires a corpus this map has not admitted.

entries.name: Prohibited or restricted areas require permission
entries.evidence: With and without permission from the using or controlling agency.
entries.note: Same shape as airspace-authorized: the designation is an input, not something derived here.

entries.name: Operation from a moving vehicle or aircraft
entries.evidence: From a moving aircraft (always prohibited); from a moving land vehicle over a sparsely populated area without carriage for hire; and the two ways the exception fails.

ambiguity.question: Part 107 does not define 'sparsely populated area', and the term carries the whole exception in (b).

entries.name: Night operation is prohibited
entries.evidence: Night, and not-night. There is no condition under which night operation is permitted.

entries.name: Operation during civil twilight
entries.evidence: Inside and outside each twilight window, with and without lighting.
entries.note: Alaska is a separate entry: the corpus defers the definition elsewhere.

entries.name: Civil twilight in Alaska
entries.evidence: Cannot be evidenced from this corpus.
entries.note: § 107.29(c)(3) fixes the meaning of Alaskan civil twilight in the Air Almanac, which this map has not admitted. Not an ambiguity: the corpus is clear, and the text that would settle it is elsewhere.

entries.name: Carriage of hazardous material
entries.evidence: Cannot be evidenced from this corpus.
entries.note: § 107.36 states the prohibition here and fixes the meaning of 'hazardous material' in 49 CFR 171.8, which this map has not admitted. Not an ambiguity: the corpus says exactly what it means and says where.

entries.name: Yielding right of way to other aircraft
entries.evidence: The assertion demanded for each of passing over, under and ahead of another aircraft; asserted and withheld; attributed to whoever made it and recorded with the outcome; and never defaulted to true when absent.
entries.note: The duty runs to every aircraft, airborne vehicle, and launch and reentry vehicle without exception, so nothing here is computed: the entry is the standard 'well clear' and nothing else, and is reclassified in place rather than split. Whether the aircraft gave way is the caller's to assert.

entries.name: Operating so close to another aircraft as to create a collision hazard
entries.evidence: The assertion asserted and withheld, attributed and recorded with the outcome, and never defaulted to true when absent.
entries.note: The corpus states a standard rather than a distance, deliberately, and § 107.37(b) is that sentence and nothing else — so the entry is reclassified in place rather than split. An engine that resolved it to a number would substitute its own rule for the corpus's.

entries.name: A covered structure or stationary vehicle provides reasonable protection from a falling small unmanned aircraft
entries.evidence: The assertion asserted and withheld for each of a covered structure and a stationary vehicle, attributed and recorded with the outcome, and never defaulted to true when absent.
entries.note: The standard qualifies the covered-structure exception; the exception itself is computable once it is asserted. Split out rather than reclassifying over-human-beings, which states a further case that needs no judgement.

entries.name: Operation over a human being
entries.evidence: The participating-person case, the covered-structure case, and a plain overflight with neither.
entries.note: One cause, not two: this version states only the participating-person and covered-structure exceptions. There is no subpart D at this date and nothing to defer to.

entries.name: Anti-collision lighting during civil twilight
entries.evidence: Fitted and unfitted, for civil twilight only. Visible for at least 3 statute miles.
entries.note: The permission to reduce intensity is the pilot's determination, not a computation.

entries.name: Visual line of sight is maintained
entries.evidence: Maintained by the remote pilot in command; maintained by a visual observer; maintained by neither.
entries.note: Whether anyone could in fact see the aircraft is not computable. The engine demands the assertion and records who made it.

entries.name: Visual observer requirements, when one is used
entries.evidence: With and without a visual observer, and with one whose communication requirement is unmet.

entries.name: Preflight familiarization, inspection and actions
entries.evidence: Each of (a) through (e) asserted and unasserted. (f) is reachable only through subpart D.
entries.note: Five obligations, (a) through (e). There is no subpart D paragraph at this date.
